newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares extend gains, more expected.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares extend gains, more expected.

text.p: Slovenia's blue-chip SBI index extended its winning streak into the fifth day on Monday and traders forecast more gains with foreign investors coming back to the market after the holidays.

"At the moment domestic demand is sufficient to push prices up. When the holidays are over prices could rise even higher as foreign activity resumes," said Matej Tomazin, a trader at brokerage Ilirija.
The SBI index rose 11.03 points or 0.70 percent to 1,587.92. Over the last five trading days the index has gained 3.46 percent.
Overall 14 shares rose, three fell and three were flat, while eight were untraded. Turnover fell to 171.7 million tolars from 245.1 million.
Trading firm Kovinotehna was the most actively traded share, firming 0.91 percent to 555 tolars on volume of 7,402 shares.
Market participants said Kovinotehna's good business results and robust outlook were pushing the share up but growth was seen limited due to the poor liquidity of the share.
Financial consultancy Finmedia was the top gainer, jumping 4.76 percent to 11,000 tolars on volume of only 15 shares.
Among the shares in the SBI index, food producer Droga was the top gainer, jumping 4.23 percent or 1,400 tolars to 34,500 tolars on volume of 59 shares.
Port operator Luka Koper led the decliners, falling 1.83 percent to 2,150 tolars on volume of 2,613 shares.
Traders expect petrol trader Petrol and issue A of drug producer Lek to remain the most attractive stocks after international investors return to the market from holidays.
Petrol rose 2.28 percent to 25,600 tolars on volume of 2,992 shares and a total turnover of 76.0 million tolars.
Lek firmed 0.11 percent to 36,040 tolars on volume of 1,392 shares with a total turnover of 50.1 million tolars.
